articles.headline: Kolkata Police issue 11-point advisory for its personnel to prevent untoward incidents at major pandals
articles.blurb: Kolkata Police said entry points to pandals will be closed when it rains and people inside will be brought out safely, with no crowd allowed inside during rain. The government has deployed nine IPS officers to handle the festive rush in Kolkata.

articles.headline: A decade on, Pink Line's UG cost hits Rs 1,000 cr/km
articles.blurb: Bengaluru Metro's 21.26-km Pink Line cost has been revised from Rs 8,730 crore in the DPR to Rs 17,346 crore, with its 13.76-km underground section costing Rs 13,876 crore (Rs 1,008.43 crore per km). Phase 2 overall is pegged at Rs 40,425 crore pending Centre assent; the Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere elevated stretch may open soon and the Dairy Circle–MG Road–Nagavara underground section is targeted by March 2027.

articles.headline: Panel proposes more health inspectors, supervisors for B'luru
articles.blurb: A committee headed by former chief secretary Vijay Bhaskar has proposed raising junior health inspectors from 115 to 369 and pourakarmika supervisors from 198 to 523 across Bengaluru's five corporations, as part of an interim report after BBMP's restructuring into the Greater Bengaluru Authority.

articles.headline: Tiger Shroff escapes assassination bid by Bishnoi gang
articles.blurb: Actor Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after three motorcycle-borne men opened fire at him in Mumbai's Juhu around 7.30 pm on Sunday; his driver Firdaus and a passerby were wounded. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility, and Juhu Police and Mumbai Crime Branch-CID launched investigations with 15 teams formed.

articles.headline: 'Like we had a war': 1,800 arrests as violent protests roil France
articles.blurb: France reeled on Sunday from Saturday's protests that saw 1,800 arrests, a historic town hall torched in Limoges and widespread looting in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities. Authorities said about 5.5 lakh people protested nationwide while organisers counted about 8 lakh; more than 500 police, gendarmes and firefighters were injured, and President Emmanuel Macron was to address the nation.

articles.headline: CJI inaugurates Ladakh bench of HC in Leh
articles.blurb: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant on Sunday inaugurated the Ladakh Bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh in Leh, which Ladakh Lt Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena called a landmark fulfilment of a long-standing demand for a court closer to home.

articles.headline: Airtel launches voice-only plans after TRAI's mandate
articles.blurb: Bharti Airtel has become the first telecom operator to roll out voice-only prepaid plans priced at Rs 185, Rs 203 and Rs 206, each offering unlimited local, STD and roaming calls and 300 SMS but no bundled mobile data, in line with TRAI norms.

articles.headline: Man arrested in stabbing incident
articles.blurb: Police on Sunday arrested Ajith Kumar Shetty, 28, after Lokesh alleged he stabbed Uday over a money dispute at Pallamajalu Junction, Bantwal taluk, on Saturday night; Uday was treated at Bantwal government hospital and shifted to Mangaluru. A case was registered at Bantwal Town Police Station under BNS Sections 118(2), 109(1) and 351(2).

articles.headline: Kudlada Pili Parba, Kinni Pili showcase the spirit of Tulu Nadu
articles.blurb: The fifth Kudlada Pili Parba at Nehru Maidan on Sunday featured 11 tiger-dance teams judged by Kadri Navaneeth Shetty and others, inaugurated by DK MP Captain Brijesh Chowta, while the second Kinni Pili competition at Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Temple drew children in tiger costumes in three categories.

articles.headline: Prof Baragur Ramachandrappa selected for Dr Shivaram Karanth Award
articles.blurb: Dr Shivaram Karanth Trust will present the Karanth Award to Prof Baragur Ramachandrappa at Dr B B Hegde First Grade College, Kundapur, on October 24 at 4 pm, alongside Karanth Special Awards to Dr P V Bhandary and others and a national seminar on re-reading Karanth's narratives.

articles.headline: Food safety officials raid bakery in Mangaluru
articles.blurb: Acting on Health Minister U T Khader's instructions, district food safety officer Dr Praveen Kumar CH raided a bakery at Falnir Junction on Saturday and seized products lacking manufacture date, expiry, batch number and FSSAI licence details.

articles.headline: 309 applications received during Praja Seva campaign
articles.blurb: District-level Praja Seva at Konaje on Saturday received 309 applications; District In-charge Minister U T Khader said the initiative brings governance closer to people and Karnataka is the only state with a dedicated Praja Seva department, while Deputy Commissioner H V Darshan said it helps clear long-pending taluk and hobli grievances.

articles.headline: Ponnu Pili performers entertain audience
articles.blurb: At Uchila Dasara at Sri Mahalakshmi Temple on Saturday, 14 teams competed in Ponnu Pili and 33 in saree categories sponsored by Mahalakshmi Cooperative Bank, with Kinni Pili winners including Viha P Suvarna (0–2 years) and Namish (4–6 years); Udupi MLA Yashpal Suvarna said women's competitions have run for four years with a separate platform for children this year.

articles.headline: Emergency evacuation during temple fairs crucial
articles.blurb: Mangaluru cardiologist Dr Padmanabh Kamath urged mandatory emergency evacuation routes at crowded festivals after a man suffered cardiac arrest during Navaratri at Kudroli Gokarnanath Temple around 8.30 pm and relatives carried him on a motorcycle through the crowd; he underwent angioplasty and is stable.

articles.headline: 'Puvempu Nenapu' and award ceremony on October 24
articles.blurb: Puvempu Nenapu honouring Dr Pundoor Venkataraja Puninchathaya will be held at Gilivindu, Manjeshwara, on October 24, with Prof Baragur Ramachandrappa receiving the 2026 Puvempu Award from Minister K H Muniyappa and Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed inaugurating the event.

articles.headline: Now, demand for a High Court bench at Udupi gains ground
articles.blurb: A Brahmavara meeting backed establishing a coastal High Court bench in Udupi, citing travel of nearly 1,000 km to Bengaluru and a population above 50 lakh across DK, Udupi and Uttara Kannada; advocate Prem Prasad Shetty welcomed the Karnataka HC chief justice's three-member feasibility committee.

articles.headline: Special drive sought to declare DK plastic-free district
articles.blurb: Former MGNREGA ombudsman Sheena Shetty petitioned District In-charge Minister U T Khader at Konaje Praja Seva to enforce the plastic ban and scientific waste disposal; Khader assured he would convene officials to work toward declaring Dakshina Kannada plastic-free.

articles.headline: Two decades on, 85% of Bengaluru's CDP roads remain on paper
articles.blurb: Roughly 1,000 km of Comprehensive Development Plan roads earmarked since the 2007 RMP remain largely unbuilt even as large housing projects were approved citing them, including a stalled 5.5-km Panathur–Gunjur–Varthur link; a mobility expert cited in the report said about 85% of promised CDP roads are still on paper amid land-acquisition and TDR disputes.

articles.headline: Dasara rush leaves commuters stranded for hours
articles.blurb: Thousands leaving Bengaluru for Dasara holidays were stuck in jams late Friday, with some reportedly on the road up to six hours on Mysuru, Tumakuru, Airport and Hosur roads; private buses were said to exit only between 3 am and 4 am on Saturday as frustrated travellers called traffic police stations.

articles.headline: Ayudha Puja at Vidhana Soudha: Govt bans chemical colours
articles.blurb: DPAR directed departments celebrating Ayudha Puja at Vidhana Soudha, Vikas Soudha and the Multi-storey building not to use chemical colours that stain heritage floors and walls, mandating natural materials and warning officers would be held accountable for damage to records and equipment.

articles.headline: Food, vaccines, med care for stray dogs
articles.blurb: Bengaluru North City Corporation said its Medi Agrahara shelter (500-dog capacity) provides nutritious food, deworming, anti-rabies vaccination and veterinary care to street dogs per Supreme Court directions, and invited public adoption under prescribed rules.

articles.headline: BMTC conducts CPR training for staff at three depots
articles.blurb: BMTC held cardiopulmonary resuscitation training with RV College of Nursing at HSR Layout, Shanthinagar and Koramangala depots for World Restart a Heart Day, planning to extend the programme across all 45 depots for drivers and conductors.

articles.headline: Six held for assaulting spa staff, extorting money
articles.blurb: Police arrested six people including four women for allegedly assaulting Vidyaranyapura spa staff on October 3, demanding ₹5 lakh and taking ₹1 lakh before being caught near KR Circle on October 6; ₹80,000 cash, phones and vehicles were seized.

articles.headline: Chemical tanker overturns, catches fire on NICE Road
articles.blurb: A Chennai–Mumbai chemical tanker overturned and caught fire near NICE Road and Kanakapura Road around 12.30 pm Sunday after a tyre burst; the driver escaped unhurt, no casualties were reported, and traffic queues stretched 2–3 km while fire crews contained the blaze.

articles.headline: Why self-injury and suicidal behaviour should not be confused
articles.blurb: Manipal Academy psychologist Dr Amandeep Singh, who secured ₹16 lakh ICSSR funding to study non-suicidal self-injury in Punjab and Karnataka, explains clinicians distinguish NSSI as emotion coping from suicidal intent and notes stigma leaves the behaviour under-reported among youth.

articles.headline: M'luru church priest arrested in Pocso case
articles.blurb: Mangaluru South Police arrested parish priest Fr Cyprian Pinto from a relative's house and remanded him in judicial custody over alleged sexual assault of a 14-year-old boy on August 14 and similar abuse of four friends; a POCSO case was registered on October 15 after the child protection directorate directed DK district officials to investigate on August 31.

articles.headline: HDK-Shivakumar rivalry revived as Cong fights 'sting' war
articles.blurb: An alleged sting targeting Siddaramaiah has deepened Congress factional rifts as H D Kumaraswamy blamed D K Shivakumar and channel owner Rakesh Shetty, while Shivakumar warned 8–10 ministers could be targeted; leaders across parties allege honey-trapping syndicates in Karnataka ahead of the 2028 Assembly election.

articles.headline: Coalition govt certain in 2028, predicts HDK
articles.blurb: Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy in Hassan on Sunday predicted a JD(S)–BJP coalition in Karnataka in 2028, alleging Priyank Kharge and the CM conspired against Siddaramaiah using sting operators and claiming NICE is the country's biggest scam.

articles.headline: BSY suspects 'conspiracy' to unseat Siddu
articles.blurb: BJP veteran B S Yediyurappa in Davangere alleged Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and others plotted to remove Siddaramaiah as chief minister and said the state government is oblivious to drought hardships facing farmers.

articles.headline: Animal welfare board circular violated, say activists
articles.blurb: Activist Snehamayi Krishna complained that Mysuru's two-day Kambala violated an AWBI circular requiring seven-day prior notification, while organisers said protocols and an AWBI observer were in place; Krishna also filed a PIL challenging free allocation of 17.5 acres at Sathagalli for a velodrome.

articles.headline: Kambala makes a splash on debut at Mysuru Dasara
articles.blurb: A two-day Kambala at Sathagalli began Sunday with 150 buffalo pairs racing on a 145 m track before CM D K Shivakumar launched the event at 7.30 pm; prizes include 16 g, 8 g and 4 g gold, about ₹3 crore government spend, honorariums of ₹65,000 and ₹50,000 per pair, and crowds topping 75,000 by noon with 20 lakh watching online by 2 pm.

articles.headline: B Y Vijayendra's meeting with Yatnal sets political tongues wagging
articles.blurb: BJP state president B Y Vijayendra and expelled MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal spoke for nearly 30 minutes at Chebbi village near Hubballi on Sunday after a campaign event, fuelling speculation about Yatnal's return to the party.

articles.headline: 'Council polls litmus test for govt'
articles.blurb: Former minister S Suresh Kumar said October 23 Graduates' and Teachers' Council elections and October 27 results would test Congress popularity, accusing the government of failing manifesto promises to graduates and teachers.

articles.headline: Kalaburagi man detained on 'terror link' suspicion
articles.blurb: Brahmapura police detained Mumtaz-Ul-Mallick from West Bengal on suspicion of Lashkar-e-Taiba social media links in a joint central-agency operation; Commissioner Sharanappa S D said one brother was released and no case was registered yet as questioning continues.

articles.headline: Rain cuts short air show, dampens crowd's sky high spirits
articles.blurb: IAF Surya Kiran's nine Hawk Mk 132 aircraft performed only about 10 minutes at Mysuru Dasara on Sunday before rain halted the Bannimantap display after three horizontal manoeuvres; the team plans a fuller Monday show.

articles.headline: Drone peacock perches Cesc at peak of success
articles.blurb: Cesc's Dasara drone show at Bannimantap used 3,473 drones to form a peacock, beating its 2025 tiger record of 2,983 drones and earning a Guinness certificate presented to technical director L Lokesh.

articles.headline: Digital attendance for outsourced, contract workers from Dec 1
articles.blurb: A circular makes Kartavya app attendance mandatory for contractual and outsourced workers from December 1, 2026, with registration by November 25 and agency bills paid only from January 1, 2027 based on app records; doctors in taluk hospitals must mark night attendance after 9 pm from November 1 on pilot.

articles.headline: Farmers' march enters Dharwad, they await response from Centre, state
articles.blurb: KRRS–Hasiru Sene's sugarcane price padayatra reached Guledakoppa in Dharwad on day five despite CM Shivakumar's talks; leaders gave Centre and state another deadline and warned of mobilising 50 lakh farmers at Yerikoppa on October 22, while HC restrained protests outside Union Minister Pralhad Joshi's residence.

articles.headline: Cane growers end hunger strike after MLA's assurance
articles.blurb: Vijayanagar sugarcane growers ended a hunger strike at Hosapete MLA H R Gaviyappa's house after he promised a post-Deepavali stakeholders' meeting on November 10 to decide on establishing a sugar factory, citing model code of conduct during Council elections.

articles.headline: Drought & cane price war may bring down sugar output by 30%
articles.blurb: Belagavi officials say drought cut sugarcane area from 7.50 lakh to 7.10 lakh hectares with yield expected to fall 30%, while price disputes delay harvest; sugar production may drop by about 5 lakh tonnes as crushing falls toward 520 lakh tonnes of cane versus 576 lakh tonnes last season.

articles.headline: No more extra work to gram panchayats: Circular
articles.blurb: RDPR directed that gram panchayats must not be assigned non-statutory work during elections, Census or disasters without RDPR consultation, citing continued violations despite 2014 and 2016 chief secretary orders.

articles.headline: 1,000 rural bus stands to be developed under VB-G RAM G
articles.blurb: RDPR Minister Eshwar Khandre directed officials to identify 1,000 high-traffic village bus stands for VB-G RAM G upgrades within 15 days to improve facilities and generate unskilled labour work.

articles.headline: Kolkata tragedy: 7 held, safety audit on
articles.blurb: After a stampede at Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity pandal in Thakurpukur killed 19 and injured over 20 on Saturday, police arrested seven including committee secretary Raj Kumar Sewda and contractor Biplab Mukherjee; CM Suvendu Adhikari sought a sitting HC judge-led SIT and announced Rs 25 lakh per deceased family, a government job for one member, Rs 5 lakh per injured and free medical care.

articles.headline: ECI's U-turn cannot erase its crimes (Opinion)
articles.blurb: The editorial says the Election Commission's Special Summary Revision in 17 SIR states admits past wrongs but cannot substitute accountability for voter exclusions, demanding searchable rolls, clarity on deleted West Bengal voters, and resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

articles.headline: Laws must punish conduct, not identity (Opinion)
articles.blurb: The editorial criticises Bengaluru police circular targeting transgender persons in public spaces, arguing BNS already covers intimidation and extortion and that profiling conflicts with Karnataka's 2017 transgender policy and 1% public job reservation.

articles.headline: Pursuing mathematics in the age of AI (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Kanadpriya Basu and Nina Atkin argue OpenAI and Anthropic claims on Navier-Stokes and Fermat build on human work with limited vetting, citing 28 Fields medallists' warning that AI benchmark races misalign with mathematics as a human creative endeavour.

articles.headline: A little hope in story land (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Teacher Vijayashanthi Murthy writes that screening WALL-E revived student empathy in her classroom, contrasting that moment with today's exhausted students who seem less moved by humour, anger or even Rohith Vemula's notes.

articles.headline: Youth anger meets State repression (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Political analyst Amaan Asim assesses CJP-led protests against ECI's SIR as channeling broad dissent but lacking seasoned organisation compared to groups like AISA, while Congress-I.N.D.I.A coordination remains limited outside Delhi.

articles.headline: Children need safe access to Internet (Opinion)
articles.blurb: C V Aravind of Bengaluru writes that while the Supreme Court upheld children's internet access as fundamental, India lacks robust monitoring and parents must supervise online activity to protect minors from criminal traps.

articles.headline: Deva's enduring melodies (Opinion)
articles.blurb: M Pradyu of Kannur mourns composer Devanesan Chokkalingam, 75, highlighting his folk-infused scores across South Indian cinema and iconic Rajinikanth soundtracks from Annamalai to Baashha.

articles.headline: SSR is good (Opinion)
articles.blurb: T V Pandarinath Naidu of Kudige welcomes the EC ordering Special Summary Revision instead of flawed SIR but asks what happens to elections already held on SIR-based rolls.

articles.headline: Climate justice and the missing rules for predictable reparation (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Thajaswini C B and Teghveer Singh discuss Nepal's August Bhote-koshi floods and shift toward compensation claims, noting Paris Agreement Article 8 excludes liability while the Loss and Damage Fund's ~$817 million pledges fall far below estimated needs.

articles.headline: The world's oldest shipwreck? Maybe. Experts urge caution
articles.blurb: Turkey announced Bronze Age amphoras off Kekova dated roughly 2,400–2,700 BC as the world's oldest shipwreck, but outside archaeologists caution the find lacks hull evidence and could be jettisoned cargo until further study of residue inside the jars.

articles.headline: Flaunting books, skipping pages (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Sumit Paul explores tsundoku and 'anti-library' psychology where unread books signal aspiration, contrasting display-only collectors with readers like Firaq Gorakhpuri and Nelson Mandela who engaged deeply with their shelves.

articles.headline: Standing alone strong (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Ananthapadmanabhan cites Dian Fossey's gorilla research and Wangari Maathai's Green Belt Movement to argue meaningful goals often begin before others understand them and require purpose-driven persistence.

articles.headline: Social, political equations: What will tilt the scales in Goa?
articles.blurb: With Goa Assembly polls due next year, analysis traces how fragmented opposition including AAP and TMC helped BJP wins, Congress hopes tribal outreach after losing South Goa in 2024, and CM Pramod Sawant seeks a third term amid shifting alliances.

articles.headline: 28 houses torched, civilians flee to forests in Manipur
articles.blurb: Police said at least 28 houses burned in Kamjong in 24 hours—13 abandoned Naga homes near Myanmar and 15 Kuki houses in Chassad—while two people were injured in shooting on NH202 in Ukhrul Sunday morning.

articles.headline: 'Conspiracy' similar to France, B'desh in India protests: Rijiju
articles.blurb: Union minister Kiren Rijiju alleged anti-India groups and politicians instigated Delhi protests on electoral roll revision like unrest in France and Bangladesh, insisting government change in India must come only through elections, not 'Soros'.

articles.headline: Month after IIT-B suicide, 22 protesters detained
articles.blurb: Police detained 22 protesters including eight twice in one day inside IIT-Bombay Powai campus Sunday, a month after Sahil Wakode's suicide; parents demand action against the director and a professor over alleged caste discrimination while Crime Branch-CID probes the death.

articles.headline: Oct 23 to witness nationwide ‘People's March’ for democracy
articles.blurb: Coalition 'People Against SIR' announced October 23 'People's March to Reclaim Democracy' nationwide demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal, scrapping SIR and restoring deleted voters, with rallies planned at tehsil to national levels without seeking police permission.

articles.headline: Cong calls for thorough rejig of Election Commission
articles.blurb: Congress's Jairam Ramesh said readable PDF electoral rolls return after eight years because of street protests, insisting CEC Gyanesh Kumar must go and the ECI IT system needs overhaul; Rahul Gandhi linked Kumar to alleged 'vote theft' with Amit Shah and PM Modi.

articles.headline: Rahul, Akhilesh, Musk depicted as Ravana in UP hoardings
articles.blurb: Sanatan Raksha Sangathan hoardings in Lucknow Sunday titled 'Ravana, Enemies of Sanatan Bharat' depicted Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Elon Musk, Prashant Bhushan, George Soros and others among Ravana's ten heads ahead of Dussehra.

articles.headline: Couldn't prevent regime change even in Shiv Sena: CM slams Uddhav
articles.blurb: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis retorted to Uddhav Thackeray's 'regime change' call by saying Thackeray could not stop splits in his own Shiv Sena after abandoning Bal Thackeray's Hindutva ideals.

articles.headline: Speaker mode on trains? Railways warns of fines, jail
articles.blurb: Indian Railways warned passengers against speaker-mode audio on trains under Railways Act Section 145(2)(a), allowing removal and Rs 1,000 fines, with up to six months' imprisonment and/or Rs 5,000 for continued violations after warning.

articles.headline: SC: Private plaints on false poll affidavits need no official nod
articles.blurb: Supreme Court held on October 16 that private citizens may file criminal complaints under Section 125-A RP Act for false nomination affidavits without ECI sanction, overturning Karnataka HC quashing of Rajkumar Madki's complaint against Bidar MLA Dr Shailendra Beldale.

articles.headline: Voters can fill Form 6 to get re-included in rolls: EC to HC
articles.blurb: Election Commission told Delhi HC that two voters deleted during SIR may file Form 6 for reinclusion; the court closed the plea, saying fears of false-declaration prosecution were misplaced when the ERO offered that route.

articles.headline: 'Only on paper': SC warns of contempt action over menstrual hygiene order
articles.blurb: Supreme Court bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and R Mahadevan gave states and UTs a final chance to report implementation of its judgment making menstrual hygiene part of Article 21 rights, threatening contempt notices to non-responsive chief secretaries and listing the matter for December 14.

articles.headline: Manager of ‘Gem’ Veeramani held; 7th Pocso case registered
articles.blurb: Chennai SIT arrested Gem Granites manager Sakthivel and registered a seventh POCSO case against granite baron R Veeramani after an eleventh minor's complaint, following raids at his Lloyd Road residence, Kanathur farmhouse and Chamundeeswari Natural Stone office.

articles.headline: HC rejects marital status bar on compassionate jobs
articles.blurb: Allahabad High Court ruled married daughters cannot be excluded from compassionate appointment solely for marital status, remitting Manisha Tyagi's Saharanpur case for fresh consideration within eight weeks after striking down 'unmarried' limits in relevant rules.

articles.headline: Assam CID to move top court challenging bail to 2 accused in Zubeen death case
articles.blurb: Assam CID will appeal Gauhati HC bail to Amritprabha Mahanta and suspended DSP Sandipan Garg in singer Zubeen Garg's September 19 Singapore drowning; CM Himanta Biswa Sarma had claimed murder though a Singapore coroner ruled drowning without foul play.

articles.headline: Flying regional skies: Connecting India’s next growth centres
articles.blurb: DH Business reports ~Rs 30,000 crore planned for 100 new airports over a decade, with regional carriers like FLY91 ordering 40 ATR 72-600 aircraft and analysts citing Modified UDAN's Rs 28,840 crore outlay while warning pilot shortages and two-way demand remain hurdles.

articles.headline: Electric car penetration likely to double to over 8% in FY27
articles.blurb: JSW MG Motor director Lakshmi Ram Kumar Subbaraj told DH EV passenger-car penetration may reach 8–8.5% this fiscal from about 4% last year, with FADA showing 36,108 EV car sales in September 2026 versus 18,559 a year earlier.

articles.headline: Crude oil likely to gain further this week
articles.blurb: Analysts expect volatile crude markets with Strait of Hormuz risks and stalled US–Iran talks; Religare's Ajit Mishra said Brent could move toward $115–120 on escalation, while MCX November crude rose 6.4% weekly to Rs 9,394 per barrel.

articles.headline: Khanal Foods moves beyond yak-cheese chews
articles.blurb: Bengaluru-based Khanal Foods targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue by 2028 from Dogsee pet treats—mostly exported to the US—and Himalayan Natives human foods, planning a Chittoor plant and discussing a Rs 300-crore fundraise after an $8-million Series B in 2025.

articles.headline: Gifting this festive season? Know the tax rules
articles.blurb: Chartered accountant B E Kumar Prasad explains Income Tax Act 2025 gift exemptions for specified relatives, Rs 50,000 annual limits for others, marriage exceptions, and clubbing rules when spouses or minor children earn from gifted assets.

articles.headline: The incredible shrinking risk: How holding periods mitigate equity volatility
articles.blurb: Rushabh Desai cites Nifty 50 TRI data from September 2000–2026 showing annualised volatility falling from 25.1% over one year to 3.5% over ten years, advising long horizons for equity goals beyond three years.

articles.headline: Nifty 50 expected to recover gradually
articles.blurb: MOFSL's Siddhartha Khemka expects Nifty consolidation above 23,000 despite FII outflows and elevated crude, with banking results and 2QFY27 earnings from HDFC Bank, Infosys and others driving sector moves this week.

articles.headline: Bengaluru leads in India's occupied office stock
articles.blurb: Knight Frank India said occupied office stock in eight leading markets rose 7% YoY to 917.7 million sq ft by September 30, 2026, with Bengaluru largest at 227.9 million sq ft (+9%) and Pune crossing 100 million sq ft.

articles.headline: 'Enterprises should own their data, avoid solutions dependent on one model'
articles.blurb: Capgemini India's Padmashree Shagrithaya tells DH firms are adopting smaller domain-specific language models for cost and sovereignty, with 93% of organisations globally discussing digital sovereignty at board level per Capgemini Research Institute.

articles.headline: India bars sugar-based ethanol in 2026-27 tender
articles.blurb: BPCL's October 16 tender for ~11 billion litres of ethanol for 20% blending excludes juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses per government directions, accepting maize, broken rice, FCI surplus rice and C-heavy molasses while cutting maize ethanol price to Rs 68.86 per litre.

articles.headline: Kolkata tragedy: ‘There’ll never be Durga Puja in our lives again’
articles.blurb: Families from Kolkata, West Bengal districts and Muzaffarpur mourned 19 stampede victims including 13-year-olds Pranjal Sarkar and Sandeep Bej at Chorebagan pandal; Barnali Haldar's rickshaw-puller father said their world had ended after the Saturday disaster.

articles.headline: TMC targets Suvendu’s nephew for stampede
articles.blurb: Trinamool Congress attacked BJP CM Suvendu Adhikari's nephew Debdeep Adhikari as chief patron of the Chorebagan committee where 19 died, noting Suvendu inaugurated the pandal on October 12 while six arrested organisers were not linked to BJP.

articles.headline: Punjab: 8 dead as car ploughs into workers
articles.blurb: Eight VB-G RAM G workers died and 12 were injured when a speeding car hit them on Lehragaga–Jakhal road near Alisher village Sunday; CM Bhagwant Mann announced Rs 2 lakh compensation per deceased as locals alleged ambulances arrived nearly an hour late.

articles.headline: GPS route in focus after Gwalior tragedy
articles.blurb: Police said truck driver Bilbagh Singh may have followed Google Maps into a no-entry zone near Sheetla Mata Temple around 1.30 am Sunday, killing 15 devotees and injuring 25+; CM Mohan Yadav ordered magisterial inquiry and suspended multiple police officials for negligence.

articles.headline: Iran urges US to accept proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
articles.blurb: Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Iran's seven-day Strait of Hormuz reopening proposal to the US remains on the table after mid-September talks stalled, conditioning progress on lifting port blockades, oil sanctions and regional hostilities.

articles.headline: Saudi skyscraper closes offices as Houthi disruption spreads
articles.blurb: Riyadh's Kingdom Centre ordered mandatory remote work for office tenants Sunday amid drone interceptions and Houthi attacks; schools extended online classes and King Khalid International Airport stayed closed after a major attack killed 13 people.

articles.headline: India asks its nationals to follow safety directives
articles.blurb: The Indian Embassy in Riyadh urged nationals to follow Saudi National Early Warning Platform instructions—seek interior rooms away from windows and stay indoors until all-clear—amid heightened Houthi strike alerts.

articles.headline: 'France is burning': Trump blames immigrants for riots
articles.blurb: US President Donald Trump on Truth Social blamed immigration for French unrest and urged closing borders; VP JD Vance linked the riots to US midterm politics as France counted 1,800 arrests after Saturday's damage including a torched Limoges town hall.

articles.headline: Pak seals temple after demolition attempt
articles.blurb: Pakistan's Evacuee Trust Property Board sealed the nearly 200-year-old Ram Leela Temple in Dera Ismail Khan on Saturday after residents stopped demolition for a commercial plaza.

articles.headline: Maldives Prez Muizzu to visit Islamabad
articles.blurb: Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu will visit Pakistan October 20–22, the first Maldivian presidential trip in nearly 11 years, marking 60 years of diplomatic relations since 1966.

articles.headline: Trump backs Netanyahu days before Israeli poll
articles.blurb: Donald Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 election, calling him a 'Great Warrior Prime Minister' after months of withholding support as their Middle East strategies diverged.

articles.headline: Europe refused to sanction China, India over Russia oil: US
articles.blurb: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US paused Russia sanctions and related tariffs on India for 60 days under the Lindsey Graham Act after European allies declined secondary sanctions on Chinese and Indian Russian oil purchases.

articles.headline: Tilak is relishing finishing games
articles.blurb: India T20I vice-captain Tilak Varma said he is adapting to Nos. 5–6 after Ishan Kishan settled at No. 3, averaging 65.66 in nine innings at No. 6 while the rain-abandoned fifth T20I against South Africa was called off in Bengaluru.

articles.headline: Karnataka’s Shashank, Priyanka triumph
articles.blurb: Shashank Patil won men's javelin gold with 76.16 m and Priyanka Madivalappa won women's 400 m hurdles in 1:00.25 at the 6th Indian Open U-23 Athletics meet in Jaipur Sunday, with Apurva Anand Naik taking bronze in the hurdles.

articles.headline: 'Bumrah shouldn't play all formats'
articles.blurb: Ravi Shastri advised Jasprit Bumrah to play Tests regularly but only sporadically in ODIs and T20Is until the ODI World Cup, as selectors rested him from New Zealand limited-overs games ahead of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

articles.headline: India canter to series victory
articles.blurb: Shafali Verma's 25-ball 55 and Smriti Mandhana's 47 not out powered India to a nine-wicket win over Zimbabwe in 8.5 overs in Raipur, sealing a 2–0 series lead after restricting Zimbabwe to 102 for 8.

articles.headline: Spain’s Chacarra charms DGC
articles.blurb: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two shots at 21-under 267 after playing 25 rain-delayed holes Sunday, leapfrogging Patrick Reed atop the Race to Dubai while Anirban Lahiri was best Indian at tied 23rd.

articles.headline: DP World extends India deal till 2035
articles.blurb: DP World confirmed title sponsorship of the DP World India Championship through 2035 under a partnership called the largest in Tour history; the USD 4 million event is co-sanctioned with PGTI.

articles.headline: Jaskaran, Chandermohan in bronze-medal bouts
articles.blurb: India's Jaskaran Singh reached the 65 kg freestyle bronze bout and Chandermohan the 79 kg bronze bout at the U23 World Wrestling Championships in Las Vegas after semifinal losses, while Rohit and Shivani remained in repechage.

articles.headline: Rain ruins opening day
articles.blurb: Scott Boland took two wickets in two balls before rain limited the Gqeberha Test to 12.2 overs Sunday, leaving South Africa 20 for 2 against Australia on day one.

articles.headline: Matata, Alemu triumph in Delhi half marathon
articles.blurb: Kenya's Charles Matata won the Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon in 58:52, breaking the 2020 course record by one second, while Ethiopia's Wudinesh Alemu took the women's title in 1:06:35 among nearly 40,000 participants.

articles.headline: Leeds hit back to hold United
articles.blurb: Dominic Calvert-Lewin's 51st-minute equaliser secured Leeds United a 1–1 Premier League draw with Manchester United after Bryan Mbeumo's 35th-minute opener at Elland Road Sunday.

articles.headline: Yamal to the fore as Barcelona trounce Betis
articles.blurb: Barcelona beat 10-man Real Betis 5–2 in Seville Saturday with Lamine Yamal among the scorers, moving five points clear atop La Liga as Hansi Flick hailed Yamal as the world's best player.

articles.headline: Fokina masters Jodar at Shanghai
articles.blurb: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina rallied from a set down to beat Rafael Jodar 1–6, 7–6 (7/5), 6–4 for his first ATP Masters 1000 title at the Shanghai Masters Sunday.

articles.headline: Chwalinska triumphs
articles.blurb: Poland's Maja Chwalinska beat Britain's Sonay Kartal 2–6, 6–4, 6–2 for her first WTA title at the Wuhan Open Sunday.

articles.headline: Manvanth saves day for hosts
articles.blurb: Manvanth Kumar's unbeaten 86 off 124 balls lifted Karnataka to 281 for 8 against Saurashtra on Ranji Trophy day one at Alur after Jaydev Unadkat (3/51) and Parth Bhut (3/73) reduced them to 187 for 7.

articles.headline: KSCA honour for Shreyas
articles.blurb: KSCA felicitated Shreyas Gopal during tea on Ranji day one at Alur for his 100th first-class appearance, presenting a jersey numbered 100 from committee member Avinash Vaidya.

articles.headline: India’s para Asiad contingent showcases 5,000 yrs of heritage
articles.blurb: Indian para athletes at the Nagoya Para Asian Games opening ceremony wore blazers featuring Indus Valley motifs and SaptSindhu collar designs, led by flag-bearers Simran Sharma and Pramod Bhagat.

articles.headline: Kirsh, Rivaan, Arshi emerge champs
articles.blurb: Krish Gupta (Senior Max), Rivaan Dev Preetham (Junior Max), Arshi Gupta (Mini Max) and Ayansh Patil (Micro Max) won MECO FMSCI National Karting titles at Meco Kartopia Bengaluru Sunday despite not winning their final races, earning World Rotax Max Grand Finals berths for three champions in Portugal November 7–14.
